notes: M4-R34: dev.tag/prod.tag are the per-env promotion gate, exactly like openclaw-version.json's fields of the same name. .github/workflows/build-hermes-image.yml pushes ONE uniquely-tagged candidate per build (h-<YYYY.M.D>-<sha7>, e.g. h-2026.9.17-abc1234) and never writes to this file -- a human lands a PR flipping dev.tag (then prod.tag, after dev validation) to an already-pushed tag; service-stack.ts reads HERMES_VERSION.dev.tag / HERMES_VERSION.prod.tag straight into AGENTCORE_HERMES_IMAGE, empty -> "" env var. prod.tag stays "" until M6. IMPORTANT: dev.tag's current value `h-v1` is a PLACEHOLDER CARRIED FROM TASK 20 AND DOES NOT EXIST IN ECR -- the workflow has never actually run, so no h-<date>-<sha> tag has been pushed yet, and the spike runtime deployed today is still on the manually-pushed `spike-m1-rc4` tag. The FIRST real run of build-hermes-image.yml produces the first genuine h-<date>-<sha7> tag (printed in its job summary); dev.tag must be flipped to that real tag in a PR BEFORE any provisioning path reads AGENTCORE_HERMES_IMAGE, or CDK will hand containers a tag ECR has never held. Also note: the Dockerfile's `RUN uv pip install --upgrade "anthropic>=1.0"` is an unpinned floating lower-bound (mirrors Dockerfile.spike as-is) -- it re-resolves to whatever the latest anthropic release is at build time, so two builds on the same base digest can still pick up different anthropic versions. Left unpinned deliberately for this task (matches the proven spike); a follow-up should pin an exact version once the SDK's bearer-mode API stabilizes.
